rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards
rows.verified: The standards promote active discussion and partnership with employees and their representatives.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards
rows.verified: The standards focus attention on underlying causes of work-related stress and their prevention.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards
rows.verified: The six areas are Demands, Control, Support, Relationships, Role and Change.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards
rows.verified: Employers have a legal duty to protect employees from stress at work by assessing risk and acting on it.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards
rows.verified: The Management Standards process includes identifying factors, identifying who may be harmed, evaluating risks, recording findings and monitoring and review.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards
rows.verified: HSE provides a workbook with checklists that can support implementation and evidence the work completed.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards
rows.verified: Work-related stress varies with job design, workload, autonomy, support, relationships, role clarity, organisational change and individual circumstances.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards
rows.verified: HSE stress guidance is organisation-, team-, role-, worker-, intervention- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level mental-health probability.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: The Demands standard covers workload, work patterns and the work environment.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: Organisations should provide adequate and achievable demands within agreed working hours.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: People's skills and abilities should be matched to job demands.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: Where possible, employees should have control over their pace of work.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: Employees should have a say over break timing and be consulted about work patterns where possible.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: Support includes information, resources and encouragement from the organisation, managers and colleagues.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: Employees should know what support is available, how to access it and how to obtain the resources needed for their jobs.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: Organisations should make role requirements clear, minimise conflicting requirements and provide a way to raise role concerns.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: Stress-control effectiveness depends on workload, staffing, management practice, worker participation, resources, job design and implementation quality.

rows.source: HSE stress demands, control, support and role
rows.verified: The Management Standards describe organisational controls and do not provide a parcel-level estimate of stress, absence or injury.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: Employers must identify what could cause injury or illness in the business.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: Employers must decide how likely harm is and how serious it could be.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: Employers must eliminate hazards where possible or otherwise control the risks.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: Risk assessment is one part of the overall process for controlling workplace risks.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: A COSHH assessment focuses on hazards and risks from hazardous substances in the workplace.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: Harmful substances can be generated by processes, including wood dust, silica dust and welding fumes.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: Labels and safety data sheets are primary inputs for identifying hazardous substances.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: COSHH assessment should consider inhalation, skin exposure and ingestion routes.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: Risk assessment outcomes depend on the actual hazard, people exposed, likelihood, severity, controls, maintenance and changing conditions.

rows.source: HSE workplace risk assessment and COSHH assessment
rows.verified: HSE risk-assessment guidance is workplace-, task-, substance-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level risk score.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment
rows.verified: Employers must protect workers from health and safety risks.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment
rows.verified: PPE must be provided free of charge when a risk assessment shows it is needed.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment
rows.verified: PPE can include helmets, gloves, eye and hearing protection, high-visibility clothing, footwear and harnesses.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment
rows.verified: Respiratory protective equipment is PPE used to reduce inhalation of dust, mist, gas or fume.
